[AMD][gfx1250] Use explicit fma in mxfp FA example (#12156)

AMD compiles with `enable_fp_fusion=False` by default, so the softmax `x
* sm_scale - m` and `l_i * alpha + l_ij` expressions were lowered to
separate packed mul and add. Use `ttgl.fma`, which now lowers to
`v_pk_fma_f32` on gfx1250.

[Gluon] Release native builder references at shutdown (#12153)

Credit to @alexk-oai (Alex Karpenko) for reporting the issue and
providing the original fix.

A JIT closure capturing a Gluon builtin can retain `GluonOpBuilder`
through semantic globals and evaluated annotations at interpreter
shutdown, producing nanobind leak warnings. Move the annotation-only
import under `TYPE_CHECKING` and postpone annotations. Both changes are
needed: deferring annotations alone or removing only the global
reference still reproduces the leak.

Validated both the PyTorch-import and native-argument-specialization
shutdown reproductions on a fresh Python 3.12 build. Both fail before
the fix and pass afterward. The Gluon frontend suite passed 604 tests
with 184 skips.

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Karpenko <alexk@openai.com>

[AMD] Fix RDNA DRAM bandwidth estimates (#11922)

`get_dram_gbps()` computes peak bandwidth as memory clock × bus width ×
2, which assumes two data transfers per clock.

The HIP driver reports the DRAM clock and bus width correctly, but current RDNA
products use GDDR6 or LPDDR5X. Their effective memory data rates require
larger transfer multipliers:

- gfx1100, gfx1101, gfx1102, gfx1200 and gfx1201 use GDDR6: 16 transfers
  per clock
- gfx1151 uses LPDDR5X: 8 transfers per clock

Use the normalized Triton target architecture to select the RDNA multiplier.
CUDA, CDNA and unknown HIP architectures retain the existing ×2 behavior.

gfx1150 and gfx1152 are intentionally excluded because their platforms
may use either DDR5 or LPDDR5X, which cannot be distinguished from the
properties currently exposed to this helper.

[AMD] Match the standalone code generator's NDEBUG to its LLVM's (#12123)

libtriton_amd_codegen is configured independently of the LLVM it links,
so
nothing makes their NDEBUG settings agree. LLVM's public headers gate
data
members on NDEBUG, so when the two disagree they lay out
MCSchedClassDesc and
ScheduleDAG differently. LLVMABIGuard.h has the details.

They are already mismatched: llvm-build.yml builds this library Release
(-DNDEBUG) against an LLVM configured -DLLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON.

This adds -UNDEBUG when the linked LLVM has assertions (-DNDEBUG when it
does
not), plus a compile-time guard so the next mismatch is a build error
instead of
a runtime one.

This is latent today: amdgpu_codegen.cc never touches MCSchedClassDesc
or
ScheduleDAG, so the wrong layout is never used. The generated AMDGCN is
byte-identical before and after, and compiling the file with -fno-inline
shows
no scheduling symbols at all. It stops being latent as soon as this
library
compiles a file that does use those types. The follow-up MIR work adds
one (https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/12122), and
with today's flags it segfaults; -UNDEBUG is what fixes it.

+//===-- LLVMABIGuard.h - Reject an LLVM layout mismatch at compile time ---===//
+//
+// This library is configured separately from the LLVM it links, so nothing
+// makes their assertion settings agree. They have to: LLVM's public headers
+// gate *data members* on bare NDEBUG, so the two sides otherwise disagree
+// about object layout.
+//
+//   struct MCSchedClassDesc       // llvm/MC/MCSchedule.h
+//     uint32_t NameOff;           // present only when !NDEBUG
+//
+//   class ScheduleDAG             // llvm/CodeGen/ScheduleDAG.h
+//     bool StressSched;           // a static constant when NDEBUG
+//
+// LLVM's own guard (llvm/Config/abi-breaking.h) does not catch this: it
+// compares LLVM_ENABLE_ABI_BREAKING_CHECKS, which comes from a generated
+// header and so reads the same on both sides whatever NDEBUG is. That macro is
+// still the right thing to test, since it records how the linked LLVM was
+// configured. A build that forces it instead of leaving the WITH_ASSERTS
+// default can define TRITON_AMD_SKIP_LLVM_ABI_GUARD and match NDEBUG itself.
+//
+// One translation unit including this is enough; it checks properties of the
+// target, not of a file.
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#ifndef TRITON_AMD_BACKEND_CODEGEN_LLVMABIGUARD_H
+#define TRITON_AMD_BACKEND_CODEGEN_LLVMABIGUARD_H
+
+#include "llvm/Config/abi-breaking.h"
+
+#ifndef TRITON_AMD_SKIP_LLVM_ABI_GUARD
+
+#if LLVM_ENABLE_ABI_BREAKING_CHECKS && defined(NDEBUG)
+#error "NDEBUG is defined but the linked LLVM was built with assertions. "    \
+       "LLVM's headers gate data members on NDEBUG, so this library and "     \
+       "libLLVM*.a would disagree about object layout. Build this library "   \
+       "with -UNDEBUG (the CMakeLists does this for you), or link an LLVM "   \
+       "built without assertions."
+#endif
+
+#if !LLVM_ENABLE_ABI_BREAKING_CHECKS && !defined(NDEBUG)
+#error "NDEBUG is not defined but the linked LLVM was built without "         \
+       "assertions. LLVM's headers gate data members on NDEBUG, so this "     \
+       "library and libLLVM*.a would disagree about object layout. Build "    \
+       "this library with -DNDEBUG (the CMakeLists does this for you), or "   \
+       "link an LLVM built with assertions."
+#endif
+
+#endif // TRITON_AMD_SKIP_LLVM_ABI_GUARD
+
+#endif // TRITON_AMD_BACKEND_CODEGEN_LLVMABIGUARD_H

[AMD][gfx1250] Support CTA-local slicing in MXFP GEMM example (#12143)

https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/12119 added multi-cta support
for basic schedules for our mxfp gemm gluon example on cdna5. This PR
adds the missing cases where we slice along a non broadcasted dimension.

Conceptually, we need to first partition the cluster-sized tensor
according to cga_layout, then slice each CTA’s local tile. However,
directly doing this in a single dimnesion will first slice the cluster
wide dimension and then split each slice across CTAs, so it's the
reverse which means we have interleaved slices on each CTA. Similarly,
concatenating accumulator subtiles along that dimension can produce an
ordering that would require cross-CTA redistribution to restore the full
tile.

Instead, the logical order of operations is fixed by reshaping the CTA
partition coordinate into a separate dimension. This lets us slice and
concatenate within each CTA’s local tile while preserving CTA ownership,
then reshape back to the cluster-wide shape.

[AMD] Use the codegen library to upgrade legacy named barriers (#12147)

Use the codegen library to upgrade legacy named barriers (ref:
https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/12145).
Since the library now handles the conversion, remove the python
address-space rewrite in `compiler.py` and always pass LLVM IR to the
library as bitcode.
Add tests for the conversion in `test_amd_codegen.py`, plus a gfx1250
compile test where two warp-specialize partitions call the same
non-inlined function. The lowering passes each partition's named barrier
handle as an extra argument, which exercises the codegen library's
conversion of function signatures and call sites.

[triton_kernels] Preserve feasible Hopper MXFP4 occupancy (#12132)

CUDA 13.3 and 13.4 ptxas can increase the register usage of
non-persistent Hopper MXFP4 matmuls enough to halve block residency. The
launch heuristic already budgets shared memory for 16 resident warps,
but only persistent kernels received the matching register constraint.

Apply the register budget to regular Hopper MXFP4 kernels when that
occupancy is feasible. Account for the accumulator footprint, available
grid waves, and the extra BF16 shared-memory tile used by scaled-input
lowering. Leave register allocation unconstrained when those resources
prevent the target, and preserve existing tile selection, pipeline
depths, and persistent-kernel behavior.

This replaces the single BF16 tile special case with a resource-based
policy; it does not change the Triton compiler, CUDA version, or
numerical operations. Regression tests check real compiled resources and
numerical results for four/eight-warp kernels, large accumulators, small
grids, and scaled inputs.

Validation on H100 with Triton fa8415bdf8 and ptxas 13.4.59:
- 13 Hopper tests pass, including the compiled-resource regressions.
- 80 numerical cases cover BF16/FP16/MXFP8 input/output paths, ragged
gather/scatter, K tails, and plain/fused SwiGLU.
- Nine compiled-resource cases pass device memcheck with zero errors;
API-error reporting is disabled for the runtime's handled capability
probe.
- 24 scaled-input controls compile to identical kernels as baseline.
- The packaged wheel passes all 13 Hopper tests; representative matmul
medians improve 18.1% plain and 4.4% with fused SwiGLU.
- Baseline/candidate comparisons verify bitwise parity; reference checks
use the existing dtype-specific tolerances.

### Controlled benchmark results

The regression is already present in ptxas 13.3; it is not specific to
the 13.3-to-13.4 update. An assembler-only comparison holds the Triton
compiler at `a34c2ab7c9700e33085aedc732352e7ce4c7ddfc`, kernel sources
at this PR's `c7f0bf56bf32c0cca58959b70b944fa41f2038f2`, PTX 8.7, H100,
driver, runtime, and random inputs fixed. Only the selected ptxas
executable changes. The baseline disables this PR's new nonpersistent
register constraint.

For the affected BF16 × MXFP4 grouped matmul (256 experts, K=2048,

[KERNELS] Support NVFP4 activations with MXFP4 weights by upcasting via MXFP8 (#12135)

## Summary

Add Blackwell matmul support for NVIDIA FP4 (NVFP4) activations and
microscaled FP4 (MXFP4) weights. Convert activation tiles to microscaled
FP8 (MXFP8) inside matmul using FP32 arithmetic, without writing
intermediate activations to global memory. This conversion adds rounding
error.

This path is currently significantly slower than MXFP8 × MXFP4 matmul.
It provides correctness support for NVFP4 activations with MXFP4
weights; performance optimization remains future work.

### Desired features

- Fused NVFP4 → MXFP8 conversion in groups of 32.
- Unswizzled or Blackwell activation-swizzled NVFP4 scales; strided or
Blackwell-swizzled MXFP4 weights.
- Plain, batched, ragged, and gathered inputs, including combined
ragged/gathered inputs.
- Outer tensor/row scales applied once in the epilogue.
- BF16 output by default, with explicit output dtypes and supplied
output tensors supported.

## Validation

Tested on NVIDIA GB300:

```bash
python -m pytest -x -s --tb=short -q \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_mxfp.py::test_nvfp4_to_mxfp8_tile \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_mxfp.py::test_nvfp4_to_mxfp8_tile_scale_pairs \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py::test_nvfp4_acts_mxfp4_weights \
  python/triton_kernels/tests/test_matmul.py::test_nvfp4_acts_mxfp4_weights_nonpersistent
```

## Lines Changed

| Type | Added | Removed | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Tests | 136 | 1 | +135 |
| Core Logic | 120 | 28 | +92 |
| AutoGenerated | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 256 | 29 | +227 |

## Reviewers Guide

- `_upcast_from_mxfp.py`: fused conversion and packed-magnitude
reduction.
- `matmul.py`, `_matmul.py`, `_p_matmul.py`: dispatch, scale loading,
gathered row bounds, and kernel integration.
- `opt_flags_nvidia.py`: shared-memory accounting for conversion.
- `test_mxfp.py`, `test_matmul.py`: regression tests.

No files are primarily movements.

[AMD] Convert legacy named barriers in the codegen library (#12145)

Triton’s LLVM emits named barrier handles in address space 3, while AMD
codegen’s LLVM (`6bc4aaf6`) includes `5bf967cb132b` and expects address
space 15. The existing python text rewrite in
`third_party/amd/backend/compiler.py` does not handle helper signatures
and call sites, causing verification failures for warp-specialized
kernels that pass barrier handles through non-inlined helpers, including
`ConSan` instrumentation.

Add `upgradeLegacyNamedBarriers` to the codegen library to convert
barrier handles and their uses through LLVM IR APIs, returning an error
for unsupported uses. A `TODO` marks the conversion for removal once
Triton’s LLVM includes `5bf967cb132b`.
